Q1: Menthol presents known hazards for dermal and eye exposure (Tier 1) based on GHS classifications. It also shows expanded hazards for environmental and inhalation exposures (Tier 2), and demonstrated low-to-moderate hazards for endocrine disruption and oral exposure (Tier 3). Data is currently deficient for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive, and organ/systemic hazards (Tier 4).
Q2: Menthol appears on both the SCIL Yellow Triangle list, indicating some hazard profile issues, and the Substances Added to Food list, suggesting its use in regulated low quantities. Its presence on the low-hazard list likely refers to tightly regulated, very low quantities, as it may still be hazardous outside those conditions.
Q3: With 10,000 literature references and a well-defined molecular structure, Menthol is extensively studied in the scientific literature, and it is not a UVCB substance. However, it lacks comprehensive, high-tier EPA toxicological assessments (IRIS/PPRTV), and some data gaps persist, particularly regarding carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive, and organ/systemic hazards, despite a moderate number of general toxicology records (18).
